articles.title: Superoptimizing an FPU emulator
articles.summary: Superoptimizing an FPU emulator is a process where a compiler automatically finds the optimal sequence for a loop-free sequence of instructions, a task that compilers are good at but struggle with non-trivial reasoning. To implement this, a function takes a float f and produces a float corresponding to the lowest set bit in f, which can be done with bit twiddling but breaks for powers of two. A brute-force approach is used to find a formula that automatically handles powers of two, but the algorithm is inefficient and prone to errors. Instead, a non-orthodox approach is used by brute-forcing all possible formulas, testing each for correctness and adding counterexamples to the list of test cases.
